prompt:
You are a sceptical financial analyst reviewing a forecast prepared by a colleague.

Given the following forecast for INFY (base year 2021):
{
  "strategy": "alt_strategy",
  "base_year": 2021,
  "anomaly_detected": true,
  "forecast": [
    {
      "year": 2022,
      "revenue_cr": 114539,
      "net_income_cr": 22350,
      "eps": 52.8
    },
    {
      "year": 2023,
      "revenue_cr": 128284,
      "net_income_cr": 25270,
      "eps": 59.9
    },
    {
      "year": 2024,
      "revenue_cr": 141112,
      "net_income_cr": 27870,
      "eps": 66.2
    }
  ],
  "top_assumptions": [
    "Digital revenue acceleration continues at 30-35% YoY, offsetting core revenue decline, driving blended consolidated revenue growth of ~12-14% in FY2022 recovering toward the pre-COVID 5-year CAGR of ~10% by FY2024, supported by large deal wins and management guidance for double-digit growth.",
    "Net profit margin sustains at approximately 19-20% of revenue as travel/visa cost savings partially reverse post-COVID normalisation (~1.5% of revenue headwind), offset by operating leverage from digital mix improvement and continued cost optimisation, keeping PAT growth broadly in line with revenue growth at ~15% in FY2022 tapering to ~10% by FY2024."
  ],
  "reasoning": "An anomaly is flagged because FY2021 reported INR revenue growth of 10.7% but constant-currency growth was only 5%, meaning a meaningful portion of the reported growth was currency tailwind rather than organic volume expansion; additionally, travel costs collapsed by ~76% (saving ~1.5% of revenue) creating a one-off margin benefit unlikely to persist. The 5-year CAGR (FY2017-FY2021) for revenues is approximately 10.1% in INR terms ((100472/68484)^(1/4)-1), and for net profit approximately 7.7%. For FY2022 a recovery-year premium of ~2-3 percentage points above the CAGR is applied given: (a) management commentary on large deal wins, 475 new customers, strong digital pipeline (digital grew 36.7%), and board-approved buyback signalling management confidence, offset by (b) second COVID wave risk in India flagged in the MD&A and partial reversal of travel-cost savings as onsite mix normalises. Growth rates are modelled at ~14% for FY2022, ~12% for FY2023, and ~10% for FY2024, mean-reverting to the long-run CAGR; EPS reflects a modest share count reduction benefit from the announced INR 9,200 crore buyback programme."
}

Step 1: Identify the 3 most critical assumptions embedded in this forecast.
Step 2: For each assumption, describe one plausible scenario where it fails.
Step 3: Rate each assumption failure as Low / Medium / High risk to the forecast accuracy.
Step 4: Assign an overall confidence score from 0-100 (100 = completely certain).

Return ONLY valid JSON:
{
  "company": "<COMPANY>",
  "base_year": <YYYY>,
  "strategy": "<baseline|alt_strategy>",
  "assumptions": [
    {"assumption": "<text>", "failure_scenario": "<text>", "risk": "<Low|Medium|High>"}
  ],
  "confidence_score": <0-100>,
  "overall_critique": "<2 sentences>"
}
